records.text: An anonymous tipster said the en-route 911 call concerning Charlie Kirk did occur, lasted three to five minutes, and continued after the caller apparently dropped the phone without realizing the call was still active.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep HZvwbfePe7o)

appearances.snippet: Tip that we received is that the call did, in fact, take place. Not only that, but it lasted anywhere from three to five minutes. ... So apparently someone phones 911 and then... ... did not engage with the 911 operator. The phone sounds as though it's dropped. It's running for approximately five minutes without the caller recognizing that it was still on.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 00:17:17 was reviewed. The sole basis is an anonymous tip relayed by Owens. No released 911 record, dispatch metadata, recording, named caller, or authoritative source was found that establishes an en-route call lasting three to five minutes or continuing after the phone was dropped. This is missing evidence, not evidence that no call occurred.

But here's where it gets super interesting. Also, allegedly, allegedly not for long, the statement, get that off of him, get that off of him is captured on this alleged 911 call.
